question: In Mendeleev's Periodic Table, at which position are the formulae of hydrides and oxides of elements written?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Top**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In Mendeleev's periodic table, the general formulas of hydrides and oxides of elements are written at the top of each group.
 
• This is done to show that all the elements in a particular group have similar chemical properties. 
 
• Mendeleev arranged elements in his periodic table based on their atomic mass and chemical properties.
 
• He observed that elements with similar properties fell into the same vertical columns, or groups.
 
• He used the similarities in the empirical formulas and properties of the compounds formed by the elements as one of the basic criteria for categorization
